title: Completeness and normalized restricted line equivalences
statement: Fix ell, E, X with ell invertible in every residue field, a completed coefficient line L with locally constant finite reduction models, and opposite-line evaluations e satisfying EvaluationFormula [def-pur-integral-line-reduction-data]. Ordinary derived tensor with every signed power preserves derived completeness for all complete unbounded inputs. Moreover Restrictions(e) holds: both ordinary and completed twists preserve the integral constructible category; their comparison is exactly the actual completion comparison; the opposite evaluations have the stated K-flat chain formulas and restrict to inverse equivalences, and the completed equivalences have exactly the displayed conjugated unit/counit equations.

Proof (3), last sentence interpreted in the derived-complete integral coefficient convention; extracted generic reduction/restriction argument

proof.text: For each signed power use signedLineTensor_equivalence to get rank one. Apply integralLineTensorComparison_iso, converting residue-field invertibility to stalk units. This is exactly IsIso of completionUnit on the ordinary tensor output. The first/fifth conditions of roosIntrinsicCompletenessEquivalence therefore imply IsComplete for that output, for every complete unbounded K. The proof constructs a good representative by the existing localization; coefficient_datum supplies the actual principal ideal, and a prime larger than l supplies the irrelevant auxiliary finite-field prime.

Obtain b and the normalized derived comparison d and support bounds from the existing power and derived comparison theorems. At each finite level the signed power has rank one by scalar extension and signedLineTensor_equivalence. On a flat-term K-flat resolution, the tensor model comparison and single-factor collapse identify its cohomology with the old cohomology tensored with that finite line. Apply finiteLineTensor_conditions to preserve constructibility and finite_ordinary_support_subset to preserve boundedness. Transport along d. Together with the completeness result and the unchanged uniform interval, this proves ordinary integral membership; transport along the actual completion comparison proves completed membership.

For each integral object, the equivalence sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy gives its existing unrestricted completeness. Thus every component of the actual comparison is invertible. Take asIso of its whiskering with the full inclusion to obtain c; its hom is definitionally the specified comparison. Use integral_line_normalized_evaluations for the two ordinary derived evaluation maps, their chain formulas, and the triangle identity.

Lift the two ordinary functors through the full subcategory. Restrict v and w by isoMk. Their triangle identity follows by faithfulness of the inclusion, giving the ordinary equivalence and the two exact evaluation equations. Keep this equivalence and compose the underlying identifications with c to identify its functors with completed tensor. Naturality of the inverse c at c.hom moves each inverse comparison next to its matching forward comparison. Cancel those pairs and the mapped forward/inverse pairs. The results are precisely the two CompletedRestriction equations. Assemble h, c, both derived evaluation formulas and both restrictions into Restrictions.

proof_origin.place: G1 2026-10-26: use the proved comparison-unit criterion for completeness; finite line cohomology and constructibility; normalized evaluations; explicit full-subcategory restriction and comparison cancellation.

lean.statement: theorem integral_line_restrictions (hl : ∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)) (L : scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X) [L.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank 1] (hfinite : FiniteReductions l E X L) (e : Evaluations l E X L) (he : EvaluationFormula l E X L e) : (∀ (m : ℤ) (K : D.{u, u} l E X none), IsComplete l E X none K → IsComplete l E X none ((ordinary l E X L m).obj K)) ∧ Restrictions l E X L e
